record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: What microscopic degrees of freedom or statistical-mechanical mechanism account for the entropy proportional to the area of cosmological event horizons, and can causal set theory identify this microscopic origin for cosmological horizon entropy?

evidence.quote: Not long after, these thermodynamic properties were extended to cosmological horizons (in models with a positive cosmological constant) as well.
Similar to the black hole case, these cosmological event horizons were also found to have a temperature and an entropy proportional to their area associated with them.
In this section we will focus on the outstanding question of: what is the microscopic origin of these (cosmological) horizon entropies?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a (3+1)-dimensional spacetime with a positive cosmological constant Λ > 0 admitting a cosmological event horizon H (for instance, the de Sitter horizon of static-patch de Sitter spacetime). Such horizons are known to behave thermodynamically: they possess a Hawking-Gibbons temperature T = (1/2π)√(Λ/3) and an entropy S = A/(4 G ℏ), where A is the horizon's area. 

Now consider the framework of causal set theory, in which a spacetime is replaced by a locally finite partially ordered set (C, ≼), where the order relation x ≼ y encodes causal precedence and the number of elements in a spacetime region is taken to be proportional to its volume (in fundamental units). A causal set approximating a continuum spacetime with cosmological horizon H induces, in particular, a discrete structure on and near H (e.g., links crossing H, or causal-set analogues of horizon "molecules").

Problem: Identify a set of microscopic degrees of freedom defined intrinsically in terms of the causal set (C, ≼) — such as elements, relations, links, or finite order-theoretic substructures localized at or near the horizon — and a statistical-mechanical counting (entropy as the logarithm of the number of microstates consistent with a suitable macroscopic horizon data) such that, in the continuum/large-N limit where the causal set approximates the given spacetime with cosmological horizon H of area A, the resulting entropy is proportional to A and reproduces S = A/(4 G ℏ). Equivalently, exhibit a causal-set statistical mechanism whose coarse-grained entropy accounts for the area law of cosmological event horizon entropy, or prove that no such mechanism exists within causal set theory.
artifact.status_search_result: The microscopic origin of cosmological horizon entropy remains an open question in quantum gravity. Within causal set theory, partial results exist (e.g., counting horizon "molecules" or maximal antichains in the spirit of Dou–Sorkin for black hole horizons, and proposals extended to de Sitter horizons), but a complete derivation reproducing the A/4 law for cosmological horizons from causal set microstates is not established.

status_evidence.title: Black hole entropy from causal sets (Dou, Sorkin)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes counting causal-set 'horizon molecules' to obtain an entropy proportional to the area of a black hole horizon; the cosmological-horizon generalization remains incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: The causal-set program for horizon entropy is still developing and the cosmological-horizon case is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Causal set approach to discrete quantum gravity (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews open problems including the microscopic origin of horizon entropy within causal set theory.
status_evidence.claim: The microscopic accounting of cosmological horizon entropy is listed as an open direction.
